docs.text: Bake Layer Data to Blender Native ¶ Click Current Bind Mesh to open a dropdown list showing all bind meshes in the scene. The model has been initialized layers with Super Skin Pro. The model has been initialized layers with Super Skin Pro but is missing the Armature Modifier. The model uses native Blender data. You can Click Bake Selected / Bake All : Bake all layer results back to native Blender. Baking Merges Layers Once baked, all layers will be merged. If you want to keep them, you can Export Weight first or don't bake. You can still share the unbaked file with anyone, even if they don't have this add-on. Editing Without Baking If you continue skinning using native Blender without baking, returning to the add-on tools will overwrite your changes with the last saved add-on state.
docs.title: Bake to Blender Native

docs.text: Bone Picker Shortcut ¶ You can select a vertex group through the Deform Bone List, but in most cases it's faster to select it directly through the Bone shown in the viewport. Hold Alt + 2 to enter Bone Picker mode. While in Bone Picker mode, you have these additional shortcuts: Pick an active Bone Select more bones Deselect bones - Release Alt + 2 : Selects whichever bone is currently hovered. - Left Click : Adds bones to the selection (multi-selection). - Middle Click : Deselects bones from the selection. - Right Click (Cancel): Cancels bone picking mode. Bone Size / Always Show Bone HUD ¶ You can now adjust the Bone Size, change the bone color, and toggle Always Show Bone HUD via the More button beside the Deform Bone List.
docs.title: Bone Picker

docs.text: Quick Start ¶ Brush Mode and Vertex Selection Mode have different available tools. In this video, you'll learn how to apply all weight operations using both brush painting and vertex selection. General Tools ¶ Weight Operation Sliders ¶ Used for adjusting weights and quickly flooding values to selected areas. Add Weight Increases weight strength. Range: 0.001 – 1.0 Scale Weight Decreases weight by multiplying it (lower = reduces more, higher = reduces less). Range: 0.0 – 0.999 Smooth Weight Blends weights smoothly. Range: 0.001 – 1.0 (can go up to 100) Sharpen Weight Sharpens weight edges. Range: 0.001 – 1.0 Note If no vertices are selected, flooding will apply to the entire mesh. Use weight step buttons to smoothly increase or decrease weight values. This makes weights easier to control and perfectly fits the feel of each weight operation. Block Weight ¶ Automatically calculates weights from the selected bones as follows: Select the bones you want to auto-assign. Click the Block Weight button. Bone Locks Block Weight pulls weight from Bones that are not Locked, so check your Bone Locks carefully for a correct Block Weight result. Face Rings When this option is checked, Block Weight follows the mesh's edge loops more closely. Watch the Face Rings example . Mirror Weight ¶ Target Side: Specifies the target side for mirroring (can be identified via the viewport HUD—the blue plane indicates the target side). Mirror Target Data: Sets whether to mirror only the Layer Mask or the Bone Weight (both by default). Use Custom Mapping Keywords (Optional): Allows you to add custom left and right side keywords for rigs with non-standard naming conventions. For most general users, there is no need to configure this setting. Multiple Layers You can select multiple layers to apply mirror weights across all of them. Selected Vertices If you have selected vertices while mirroring, the mirror will only apply to the selected vertices. Copy Weight ¶ Copy weights from the active vertex group to the clipboard. Steps: Copy or Cut: Copy or cut the weights from the current vertex group. Paste: Select the target bone or layer mask, then paste the weights (choose between Add, Replace, or Subtract). Note You can copy and paste across bone and mask modes. Multi-Color Preview ¶ While in Bone Mode, press Alt + 3 to toggle Multi-Color Preview. Note Multi-Color mode may impact performance. Keep Volume ¶ When Keep Volume is enabled, it automatically maintains mesh distance and seamlessly connects separated seams. Ideal for clothing or multi-part meshes. Keep Volume works in all modes—whether you are using brush paint, vertex selection, or clicking flood weight from the N-panel. When Keep Volume is enabled in vertex mode, you can select vertices across connected seams as if they were a single mesh. Brush Mode Tools ¶ Brush Shortcut ¶ Brush Options ¶ Brush Mode - Right Click Popup Option Brush Falloff ¶ You can change the falloff type for the surface brush and projected brush. There are 3 presets: constant, smooth, and linear. Connected Only Option for Brush ¶ Check the "Connected Only" option to limit weight painting to connected surface parts only. Vertex Mode Tools ¶ Vertex Paint Weight Gesture ¶ Hold Alt + Left Click and drag left to Scale Weight Hold Alt + Left Click and drag right to Add Weight Hold Alt + Right Click and drag left to Sharpen Weight Hold Alt + Right Click and drag right to Smooth Weight Note If no vertices are selected, this will apply to the entire mesh. Vertex Options ¶ Vertex Mode - Right Click Popup Option Self Transfer ¶ Transfers weight from a Vertex within the same Mesh , as follows: Select the Vertex to use as the Source, press Self Transfer... , then press Mark Source in the popup Select the target Vertex (Target), press Self Transfer... again, then press Transfer in the popup Transfer Target The transfer operation affects both bone and mask data of the active layer. Copy Vertex Weight ¶ Copy the weight values of a selected vertex to the clipboard. Steps: Select a single vertex, then click Copy Vertex to copy its weight data to the clipboard. Select the target vertices, then click Paste Vertex to apply the weights. Note You can copy and paste across bone and mask modes. Hammer Weight ¶ Click the Hammer button to hammer selected vertices to average their weights.
docs.title: Paint Weight Tools

docs.text: FAQ (Frequently Asked Questions) ¶ Learning the Add-on ¶ I've never done layer-based weight painting before. What can it do? Think of it like Photoshop layers, but for skin weights. You can fix parts without breaking your old work, mix weights together, or even paint weights from scratch. Where should I start learning the layer-based workflow? We recommend starting with our YouTube Tutorial Playlist . If you want to read more details, check out our Full Documentation . Add-on Compatibility ¶ Does this add-on work with any rig? Yes, absolutely. The add-on only paints weights and doesn't change your rig. You can use it with any rig, including custom rigs, Rigify, or Auto-Rig Pro. Will my skin weights work for people who don't have this add-on? Yes. Other people can open and use your .blend files normally, even if they don't have this add-on. Are future updates free? Free Lifetime Updates. Buy it once, and all future updates (bug fixes and new tools) are free to download from your Gumroad Library. If I update to a newer version, will my older files still work? Yes. Old files will still work fine. Updating the add-on will not break or change your saved weights. Does the add-on support custom shortcuts? Yes. Go to the add-on panel, then click Settings > Edit Shortcuts . Which Blender versions does the Add-on support? Supports Blender 4.2, 4.5, 5.0, and 5.2. Support & Community ¶ How do I get help or report bugs? Join the Super Skin Pro Discord Server to chat, ask questions, or report bugs. Are there any plans for new features? Do you accept feature requests? Yes! Right now, my main goal is fixing bugs and making sure everything runs smoothly. But I'm always happy to hear your ideas! I will check every request to see if it helps most users. Feel free to share your thoughts in our Super Skin Pro Discord Server Add-on Limitations ¶ Blender's Native Skinning Tools Please use the add-on's own tools (Mirror, Transfer, Smooth/Brush, and Vertex Selection) instead of Blender's default tools while working with layers. Watch the Brush & Vertex Selection tutorial . Baking to Native Blender You can bake your weights back to normal Blender anytime: Baking Documentation (Note: baking merges all layers together). To keep things easy to edit, we recommend keeping your layers until your project is finished. Modifier Stack Order When skinning, try not to put heavy deformation modifiers above the Armature modifier in the list.
docs.title: FAQ

docs.text: Drag-and-Drop Installation ¶ Download the SuperSkinPro .zip file from Gumroad . Open Blender , drag and drop the .zip file directly into the Blender viewport/window, and confirm the installation. Restart Blender after installing or updating the add-on. Once installed, SuperSkinPro will appear in the N-Panel sidebar. Always Restart Blender After Updating or Reinstalling If you update or reinstall the add-on, you must always restart Blender afterward to ensure the add-on works properly. How to Update ¶ When a new update is released, you can redownload the latest SuperSkinPro files from your Gumroad Library and repeat the installation steps above.
docs.title: How to Install

docs.text: Object Mode Tools ¶ Weight Transfer ¶ Weight transfer supports any number of source and target meshes. It can be used in various ways, such as: 1) Transfer weights from the body to clothing and accessories ¶ How to use: Add both the body and clothing to the Transfer list. Mark the body mesh as Source . Click Transfer Weight . 2) Transfer weights from multiple meshes ¶ How to use: Add the source meshes and the target mesh to the Transfer list. Mark the relevant meshes as Source . Click Transfer Weight . 3) And much more as demonstrated in the video ¶ Other Transfer Options: You can restrict the transfer to specific source or target areas by enabling the Use Selected Vertices Only toggle (the selection must exist in Edit Mode). If the target already has a layer system, the output will be added as a new layer named "Transfer Output". Enabling the Force Target to Init Layer checkbox forces layer data initialization for all target meshes if they are still using native vertex groups. Armature Parenting Target meshes do not need to be parented to an armature beforehand, as the tool will automatically parent them during the transfer. However, the source mesh must always be parented to an armature first . Weight Export ¶ Export all layer data and skin weights from a selected mesh to a file. How to use: Select the mesh you want to export layer data from. Click Export Weights . Weight Import ¶ How to use: Select the target mesh you want to import weights to. Click Import Weights . Options: Transfer Method: Choose a weight transfer method during import, such as Closest Distance or Vertex ID . Preserve Existing Layers: Check this option to keep current layers on the mesh. (This option only appears if the target mesh already has layer data.)
docs.title: Object Mode Tools

docs.text: 1.2.3 ¶ 1.2.3 Fixed: "Smooth Affected Only" had no effect on a full selection and could spread weight further on a partial one. Smooth now keeps empty vertices empty and adds no new bones to a vertex. 1.2.2 ¶ 1.2.2 Surface Brush ¶ Improved: Surface Brush: Automatically isolates front and back surfaces to prevent weight bleeding while brushing. Keep Volume ¶ Improved: Resolved depth conflicts so the innermost layer always leads and layers never swap roles, preventing the ping-pong effect. Improved: "Connected Only" option now maintains Keep Volume independently per piece. Changed: Brushes and selections now strictly affect vertices within their bounds. Fixed: Sharpen Weight brush no longer breaks seam welds when Keep Volume is enabled. Others ¶ Improved: "Mirror All Layers" and "Always Show Bone HUD" settings now save app-wide (Preferences). Improved: "Front Face Only (Lasso)", "Sync with Edit Mode Selection", "Move Weight by Name", and "Limit Total's Max Influences" settings now save per scene in the .blend file. 1.2.1 ¶ 1.2.1 Added: "Sync with Edit Mode Selection" in Vertex Mode header to share selection and hidden vertices with Edit Mode. Improved: Deform bone selection sync across Pose Mode and Weight Paint. Improved: Independent Strength Pressure for Surface (On by default) and Projected brushes (Off by default). Fixed: Resolved shortcut conflicts with native Blender tools—now restricted to Brush and Vertex modes. 1.2.0 ( Minor Update ) ¶ 1.2.0 ( Minor Update ) Brush Paint Update ¶ - Falloff Preset ¶ You can now change the falloff type for surface brush and projected brush. There are 3 presets: constant, smooth, and linear. Removed Options Old falloff pressure and falloff sliders have been removed. Removed size pressure since strength pressure is usually enough for weight painting. - Connected Only Option for Brush ¶ You can now check the "Connected Only" option. This limits your weight painting to only affect the connected surface parts. - Support Off-Mesh Painting when using Surface Brush ¶ Surface brush can now be used even when the brush cursor is outside the mesh. This helps you fine-tune silhouettes much easier. - Brush HUD Color Customization ¶ Now you can change cursor colors in the cursor dropdown menu. Enhanced Sharpen Weight ¶ The new sharpen weight has been heavily improved. New Behavior: Keep Volume ¶ - Easily Paint Weight Clothes! ¶ When Keep Volume is on, it automatically keeps mesh distance and connects separated seams nicely. - Supports both Brush and Vertex modes ¶ Keep volume works in all modes—whether you are using brush paint, vertex selection, or clicking flood weight from the N-panel. - Keep Separate Surface Selection as One ¶ When keep volume is enabled, you can select vertices across connected seams as if they were a single mesh. UX&UI Improvement ¶ - Update Behavior Across Vertex Selection and Brush Mode ¶ hammer weight, self transfer, and copy vertex weight will now only show up in vertex mode. If you have a vertex selection and switch to brush mode, it will automatically isolate the selected area. Note To keep things clean, we removed add vertex selection, remove selection, and hide/unhide mesh features from brush mode. Those tasks now belong fully to vertex mode. - Weight Steps ¶ Added step buttons for sliders in the N-panel. Use weight step buttons to smoothly increase or decrease weight values. This makes weights easier to control and perfectly fits the feel of each weight operation. - Refine Slider Pop-up UI ¶ Brush Mode - Right Click Popup Weight Slider Vertex Mode - Right Click Popup Weight Slider - Select Multiple Bones Faster with Lasso ¶ Click and drag around the bones to automatically use lasso selection. - Add Bone HUD Color Customization ¶ You now can set the color of bones HUD. - Add Mirror to All Layers Option ¶ Added a "mirror to all layers" option. Since most characters are symmetrical, turning this on ensures you never forget to mirror other layers and saves time from having to select every layer manually. - Add Show Shortcut Hint Option ¶ You can now toggle shortcut hints on and off through the add-on settings button. Other Improvements ¶ Improved smooth weight to work much better on dense topology meshes without needing overly high smooth settings. Improved the block weight algorithm for the face ring option. Improved the UI so self-transfer is easier to use without needing to toggle out to set a new source. Improved camera rotation to be more easier to control. Improved mirror weight performance. Removed smooth and repeat options from block weight since they duplicated the regular smooth buttons in the N-panel. Fixed a bug where block weight popups could not edit past values if a bone was selected after using block weight. Fixed the right-click popup in brush and vertex modes where settings would close immediately after changing them. Fixed shortcut bugs where add-on shortcuts leaked into native Blender weight paint mode. Fixed vertex weight operation gestures to be more compatible with pen tablets. Prevented native brush settings popups from showing up when pressing Alt+F, Shift+F, or Ctrl+F. 1.1.7 ¶ 1.1.7 Fixed: While weight painting, orbiting now rotates around the bone you last selected or the spot you last painted. Fixed: The Bake popup is shorter and narrower, with a Bake button instead of OK. Improved viewport orbiting around selection in v1.1.7 1.1.6 ¶ 1.1.6 Fixed: with Orbit Around Selection turned on, orbiting during weight painting rotated around the character’s origin. It now rotates around the view center. 1.1.5 ¶ 1.1.5 Fixed: Pressing Numpad . during Weight Paint mode now centers the view on the mesh weighted to the active bone, allowing orbiting directly around that bone. Fixed: The Bone HUD skeleton is now rendered beneath the viewport HUD text to keep the text readable. 1.1.4 ¶ 1.1.4 Fixed: Importing weights no longer opens the file browser a second time after the import completes. Import now opens the file browser directly. Import settings (Method, Preserve Existing Layers) are in an Options section of the file browser's side panel. Import and Export are only enabled when a mesh is selected in the viewport. Export also requires the mesh to contain layer data. 1.1.3 ¶ 1.1.3 Add, Scale and Smooth now show a warning in the status bar when weight could not be distributed or pulled from other bones, or when Smooth found nothing to change, with a hint that some bones may be locked Edit Weight Mode now shows how many vertices are hidden at the bottom of the viewport until they are revealed The Deform Bones list is now locked outside Edit Weight Mode and can only be used while editing weights Select Locked and Select Unlocked now show a message when no bone matches Fixed Select Locked and Select Unlocked clearing the current bone selection when no bone matched Fixed the add-on panel shifting up slightly when switching to Pose Mode 1.1.2 ¶ 1.1.2 Improve toast HUD for Limit Total, Normalize, and Selection tools Fix "Weight brush not found" warning when entering Weight Paint mode Add documentation link to the add-on manifest and remove the Gumroad link button from the UI 1.1.1 ¶ 1.1.1 Restore the "Preserve Existing Layers" option in the Import Weight dialog 1.1.0 ( Minor Update ) ¶ 1.1.0 ( Minor Update ) Mirror Weight Settings Update ¶ Since Blender mostly mirrors in the X-axis anyway, we made the mirror weight options simpler. Added a target side HUD preview: the blue plane area shows the target side for mirroring. The "Use Custom Keywords" option is now an optional setting, intended only for users who use keywords that differ greatly from the standard ones. General users no longer need to configure this. Bone Hud Update ¶ Improved the Bone HUD display to make it clearer to see. Added an option for "Always show bone display" to keep the Bone HUD visible all the time, located in the More Button next to the Deform Bone List (enabled by default). Moved the option for adjusting Bone Size into the More Button of the Deform Bone List as well. Selection Update ¶ Added options to select unaffected vertices / deselect unaffected vertices for greater flexibility in use. Others Bug fix and improve ¶ We improved the Transfer Weight options and behavior to make them easier to understand. You can read more in Weight Transfer The Transfer Weight list and Active Mesh list now support selecting multiple items at once. Improved the system so it can smooth between existing bone weights and empty weight areas. Now supports Apple M-Series. Improved the popup width to auto-size according to the item names automatically. Improved icons to clearly distinguish between meshes using layer-based skin weights and native weights. 1.0.13 ¶ 1.0.13 Weight Transfer fix: when “Use Selected Vertices Only” is on for the source, the mask is now taken from the same selected area as the weight. Before, it could come from the nearest unselected area. Improved Mask Color to see more clear. Fix deform bone list , weight color display error when amarture have no deform bones 1.0.12 ¶ 1.0.12 Improved performance when applying weights. Fixed skin weights breaking after editing meshes. 1.0.11 ¶ 1.0.11 Entering Blender's native Weight Paint Mode no longer forces the add-on mode, preserving standard workflows for non-deform vertex groups. 1.0.10 ¶ 1.0.10 Added a status for meshes with layer data but missing an armature modifer. Added pressure sensitivity toggles for brush size, hardness, and strength. Added a Normalize Weights button to the Limit Total popup. Increased the maximum brush size limit for surface brushes. Fixed an issue where applying weights affected non-deform vertex groups. (Crucial Bug) 1.0.9 ¶ 1.0.9 Added a button to switch to Object Mode. Added a fade-out effect when exit from Bone Picker. Added a Clear button to the Transfer Settings popup. Improved add-on performance when switching layers and smoothing weights. Fixed Armature not hiding when entering Weight Paint mode. Fixed Smoothing weight error when increast to extreme values. 1.0.8 ¶ 1.0.8 Major UI redesign. Added shortcut customization to the Settings button. Added new features: "Set Total" (limit max bone influences) and "Hammer" (average vertex weights). Removed auto-update feature. Improve add-on performances. 1.0.7 ¶ 1.0.7 Improved the bind mesh dropdown in the List Viewer to be easier to use — see Clean-up Layer Data for details. Improved the Weight Transfer interface to be easier to use. 1.0.6 ¶ 1.0.6 Shortcut Guide: Press Alt + 4 while editing to toggle the Shortcut Guide. Mask Edit Toggle: Press Alt + 1 while editing to toggle Mask Edit mode. Selection Persistence: Exiting Mask Edit mode now preserves all active selections in the Deform Bone list. Repeat Last Operation: Added support for Shift + R to repeat the most recent Apply Weight operation. UI Improvements: Enhanced the user interface for both the Layer List and Deform Bone List sections. Bug Fixes : Multi-Color Mode: Fixed display updates to ensure higher accuracy when using Mirror Weight and Auto Assign Weight. Scale Weight Distribution: Improved the scaling behavior to distribute weight more intelligently based on the rig hierarchy. 1.0.5 ¶ 1.0.5 Bone Picker now shows a header text indicating that bone picking mode is active. Bone Picker now displays the name of the hovered bone. Bone Picker has a redesigned color scheme for showing bone selection status. Improved performance when hovering bones with Multi Color mode enabled. Extended add-on support to Blender 4.2 LTS and newer. Bug Fixes : Fixed the Viewport Overlay not being restored when exiting Edit Weight mode back to the user's normal edit mode. Fixed the Initialize system running again automatically when selecting a mesh.
docs.title: Release Notes

docs.text: 1.2.3 Fixed: "Smooth Affected Only" had no effect on a full selection and could spread weight further on a partial one. Smooth now keeps empty vertices empty and adds no new bones to a vertex.
Improved: Surface Brush: Automatically isolates front and back surfaces to prevent weight bleeding while brushing.
docs.title: Surface Brush

docs.text: Improved: Resolved depth conflicts so the innermost layer always leads and layers never swap roles, preventing the ping-pong effect. Improved: "Connected Only" option now maintains Keep Volume independently per piece. Changed: Brushes and selections now strictly affect vertices within their bounds. Fixed: Sharpen Weight brush no longer breaks seam welds when Keep Volume is enabled.
docs.title: Keep Volume

docs.text: Improved: "Mirror All Layers" and "Always Show Bone HUD" settings now save app-wide (Preferences). Improved: "Front Face Only (Lasso)", "Sync with Edit Mode Selection", "Move Weight by Name", and "Limit Total's Max Influences" settings now save per scene in the .blend file.
docs.title: Others

docs.text: 1.2.1 Added: "Sync with Edit Mode Selection" in Vertex Mode header to share selection and hidden vertices with Edit Mode. Improved: Deform bone selection sync across Pose Mode and Weight Paint. Improved: Independent Strength Pressure for Surface (On by default) and Projected brushes (Off by default). Fixed: Resolved shortcut conflicts with native Blender tools—now restricted to Brush and Vertex modes.
1.2.0 ( Minor Update )
docs.title: 1.2.0 ( Minor Update )

docs.text: You can now change the falloff type for surface brush and projected brush. There are 3 presets: constant, smooth, and linear. Removed Options Old falloff pressure and falloff sliders have been removed. Removed size pressure since strength pressure is usually enough for weight painting.
docs.title: - Falloff Preset

docs.text: You can now check the "Connected Only" option. This limits your weight painting to only affect the connected surface parts.
docs.title: - Connected Only Option for Brush

docs.text: Surface brush can now be used even when the brush cursor is outside the mesh. This helps you fine-tune silhouettes much easier.
docs.title: - Support Off-Mesh Painting when using Surface Brush

docs.text: Now you can change cursor colors in the cursor dropdown menu.
docs.title: - Brush HUD Color Customization

docs.text: The new sharpen weight has been heavily improved.
docs.title: Enhanced Sharpen Weight

docs.text: When Keep Volume is on, it automatically keeps mesh distance and connects separated seams nicely.
docs.title: - Easily Paint Weight Clothes!

docs.text: Keep volume works in all modes—whether you are using brush paint, vertex selection, or clicking flood weight from the N-panel.
docs.title: - Supports both Brush and Vertex modes

docs.text: When keep volume is enabled, you can select vertices across connected seams as if they were a single mesh.
docs.title: - Keep Separate Surface Selection as One

docs.text: hammer weight, self transfer, and copy vertex weight will now only show up in vertex mode. If you have a vertex selection and switch to brush mode, it will automatically isolate the selected area. Note To keep things clean, we removed add vertex selection, remove selection, and hide/unhide mesh features from brush mode. Those tasks now belong fully to vertex mode.
docs.title: - Update Behavior Across Vertex Selection and Brush Mode

docs.text: Added step buttons for sliders in the N-panel. Use weight step buttons to smoothly increase or decrease weight values. This makes weights easier to control and perfectly fits the feel of each weight operation.
docs.title: - Weight Steps

docs.text: Brush Mode - Right Click Popup Weight Slider Vertex Mode - Right Click Popup Weight Slider
docs.title: - Refine Slider Pop-up UI

docs.text: Click and drag around the bones to automatically use lasso selection.
docs.title: - Select Multiple Bones Faster with Lasso

docs.text: You now can set the color of bones HUD.
docs.title: - Add Bone HUD Color Customization

docs.text: Added a "mirror to all layers" option. Since most characters are symmetrical, turning this on ensures you never forget to mirror other layers and saves time from having to select every layer manually.
docs.title: - Add Mirror to All Layers Option

docs.text: You can now toggle shortcut hints on and off through the add-on settings button.
docs.title: - Add Show Shortcut Hint Option

docs.text: Improved smooth weight to work much better on dense topology meshes without needing overly high smooth settings. Improved the block weight algorithm for the face ring option. Improved the UI so self-transfer is easier to use without needing to toggle out to set a new source. Improved camera rotation to be more easier to control. Improved mirror weight performance. Removed smooth and repeat options from block weight since they duplicated the regular smooth buttons in the N-panel. Fixed a bug where block weight popups could not edit past values if a bone was selected after using block weight. Fixed the right-click popup in brush and vertex modes where settings would close immediately after changing them. Fixed shortcut bugs where add-on shortcuts leaked into native Blender weight paint mode. Fixed vertex weight operation gestures to be more compatible with pen tablets. Prevented native brush settings popups from showing up when pressing Alt+F, Shift+F, or Ctrl+F.
docs.title: Other Improvements

docs.text: 1.1.7 Fixed: While weight painting, orbiting now rotates around the bone you last selected or the spot you last painted. Fixed: The Bake popup is shorter and narrower, with a Bake button instead of OK. Improved viewport orbiting around selection in v1.1.7
1.1.6 Fixed: with Orbit Around Selection turned on, orbiting during weight painting rotated around the character’s origin. It now rotates around the view center.

1.1.5 Fixed: Pressing Numpad . during Weight Paint mode now centers the view on the mesh weighted to the active bone, allowing orbiting directly around that bone. Fixed: The Bone HUD skeleton is now rendered beneath the viewport HUD text to keep the text readable.

1.1.4 Fixed: Importing weights no longer opens the file browser a second time after the import completes. Import now opens the file browser directly. Import settings (Method, Preserve Existing Layers) are in an Options section of the file browser's side panel. Import and Export are only enabled when a mesh is selected in the viewport. Export also requires the mesh to contain layer data.

1.1.3 Add, Scale and Smooth now show a warning in the status bar when weight could not be distributed or pulled from other bones, or when Smooth found nothing to change, with a hint that some bones may be locked Edit Weight Mode now shows how many vertices are hidden at the bottom of the viewport until they are revealed The Deform Bones list is now locked outside Edit Weight Mode and can only be used while editing weights Select Locked and Select Unlocked now show a message when no bone matches Fixed Select Locked and Select Unlocked clearing the current bone selection when no bone matched Fixed the add-on panel shifting up slightly when switching to Pose Mode

1.1.2 Improve toast HUD for Limit Total, Normalize, and Selection tools Fix "Weight brush not found" warning when entering Weight Paint mode Add documentation link to the add-on manifest and remove the Gumroad link button from the UI
1.1.1 Restore the "Preserve Existing Layers" option in the Import Weight dialog
1.1.0 ( Minor Update )
docs.title: 1.1.0 ( Minor Update )

docs.text: Since Blender mostly mirrors in the X-axis anyway, we made the mirror weight options simpler. Added a target side HUD preview: the blue plane area shows the target side for mirroring. The "Use Custom Keywords" option is now an optional setting, intended only for users who use keywords that differ greatly from the standard ones. General users no longer need to configure this.
docs.title: Mirror Weight Settings Update

docs.text: Improved the Bone HUD display to make it clearer to see. Added an option for "Always show bone display" to keep the Bone HUD visible all the time, located in the More Button next to the Deform Bone List (enabled by default). Moved the option for adjusting Bone Size into the More Button of the Deform Bone List as well.
docs.title: Bone Hud Update

docs.text: Added options to select unaffected vertices / deselect unaffected vertices for greater flexibility in use.
docs.title: Selection Update

docs.text: We improved the Transfer Weight options and behavior to make them easier to understand. You can read more in Weight Transfer The Transfer Weight list and Active Mesh list now support selecting multiple items at once. Improved the system so it can smooth between existing bone weights and empty weight areas. Now supports Apple M-Series. Improved the popup width to auto-size according to the item names automatically. Improved icons to clearly distinguish between meshes using layer-based skin weights and native weights.
docs.title: Others Bug fix and improve

docs.text: 1.0.13 Weight Transfer fix: when “Use Selected Vertices Only” is on for the source, the mask is now taken from the same selected area as the weight. Before, it could come from the nearest unselected area. Improved Mask Color to see more clear. Fix deform bone list , weight color display error when amarture have no deform bones
1.0.12 Improved performance when applying weights. Fixed skin weights breaking after editing meshes.
1.0.11 Entering Blender's native Weight Paint Mode no longer forces the add-on mode, preserving standard workflows for non-deform vertex groups.

1.0.10 Added a status for meshes with layer data but missing an armature modifer. Added pressure sensitivity toggles for brush size, hardness, and strength. Added a Normalize Weights button to the Limit Total popup. Increased the maximum brush size limit for surface brushes. Fixed an issue where applying weights affected non-deform vertex groups. (Crucial Bug)

1.0.9 Added a button to switch to Object Mode. Added a fade-out effect when exit from Bone Picker. Added a Clear button to the Transfer Settings popup. Improved add-on performance when switching layers and smoothing weights. Fixed Armature not hiding when entering Weight Paint mode. Fixed Smoothing weight error when increast to extreme values.

1.0.8 Major UI redesign. Added shortcut customization to the Settings button. Added new features: "Set Total" (limit max bone influences) and "Hammer" (average vertex weights). Removed auto-update feature. Improve add-on performances.
1.0.7 Improved the bind mesh dropdown in the List Viewer to be easier to use — see Clean-up Layer Data for details. Improved the Weight Transfer interface to be easier to use.

1.0.6 Shortcut Guide: Press Alt + 4 while editing to toggle the Shortcut Guide. Mask Edit Toggle: Press Alt + 1 while editing to toggle Mask Edit mode. Selection Persistence: Exiting Mask Edit mode now preserves all active selections in the Deform Bone list. Repeat Last Operation: Added support for Shift + R to repeat the most recent Apply Weight operation. UI Improvements: Enhanced the user interface for both the Layer List and Deform Bone List sections. Bug Fixes : Multi-Color Mode: Fixed display updates to ensure higher accuracy when using Mirror Weight and Auto Assign Weight. Scale Weight Distribution: Improved the scaling behavior to distribute weight more intelligently based on the rig hierarchy.

1.0.5 Bone Picker now shows a header text indicating that bone picking mode is active. Bone Picker now displays the name of the hovered bone. Bone Picker has a redesigned color scheme for showing bone selection status. Improved performance when hovering bones with Multi Color mode enabled. Extended add-on support to Blender 4.2 LTS and newer. Bug Fixes : Fixed the Viewport Overlay not being restored when exiting Edit Weight mode back to the user's normal edit mode. Fixed the Initialize system running again automatically when selecting a mesh.

Quick Start ¶ For a quick guide on how to use the add-on, watching all the videos in this playlist should be more than enough to get you started: 👉 Watch Super Skin Pro Tutorials Playlist Super Skin Pro YouTube Tutorial Playlist by tomatactics In the next section below, we’ll take an in-depth look at the interface and its features. Interface Overview ¶ 1) Active Bind Mesh ¶ Displays the currently selected mesh and provides the option to Bake Layer Data to Blender Native . 2) Layer List ¶ Displays all skin weight layers. You can add, delete, reorder, duplicate, merge, and toggle the visibility of each layer. Watch Layer Tutorial Enable / Disable: Toggle layer activation by clicking the icon in front of the layer item. Rename: Double-click the layer name to rename it. 3) Bone List ¶ Displays the active deform bones for the selected layer. Lock / Unlock: Click the lock icon in front of any bone to prevent weight bleeding . Focus Viewport: Double-click a bone to focus on it in the 3D viewport. Filter Influenced Bones: Toggle via the button in the right menu to display only bones with weights. Viewport Bone Selection In Weight Paint Mode, you can select bones through the viewport . List Shortcuts Both the bone and layer lists support the following shortcuts: Ctrl + Click : Add or remove items individually Shift + Click : Select a range of items Ctrl + A or Alt + Shift + Click : Select all items in the list Ctrl + I : Invert selection 4) Mode Switcher ¶ Quick buttons for switching between Object Mode, Weight Paint (Brush), Weight Paint (Vertex Selection), and Pose Mode. 5) Mode Tools ¶ Tools available for each mode: 👉 Read More Details on Object Mode Tools 👉 Read More Details on Weight Paint Mode Tools
